Graduate Admissions Information
Thank you for your interest in our Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering Department graduate programs!
We encourage you to read through the information below to learn detailed information about our PhD and MS programs, view our webinars, and learn about our application process and deadlines.
If you still have questions, please contact ecegrad@colorado.edu
Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering Graduate Programs
Doctor of Philosophy
Contribute original discoveries and advancements to the field as you prepare for a career in research, academia or industry.
Master of Science
Our traditional master’s degree prepares students for a successful career in academia or industry. Students are admitted to the coursework-only track that allows them to build-their-own-degree based on their interests. A thesis track is optional.
Professional Master of Science
Our subplan-based master’s option is tailored for working professionals to help advance their careers in five industry-specific fields. Many course are taught by lecturers with advanced and specific industry experience.
Online Master of Science
Our online MS program offers stackable graduate-level courses, graduate certificates, and a fully accredited master’s degree in electrical and computer engineering hosted on Coursera.
Certificates
Explore interdisciplinary skills related to electrical and computer engineering without pursuing a full degree.

Deadlines & Decisions
We have two annual admission cycles, Fall and Spring. There is no admission for Summer.
The application cycle opens annually in late July for both Fall and Spring.
All application materials must be received by the application deadline for the application to move forward in the review process. Late applications are not accepted and the application fee is non-refundable.
Twenty-four hours after you receive the email confirming that your application was successfully submitted, you will be able to check your application status using the same login credentials as the application in your Application Portal.
We do not review any applications until after the application deadline has passed. Decisions are made after careful consideration of all applicants. Decisions are not issued in the order an application was received. You are encouraged to check your application status on that portal, because there will be no follow up emails while applications are being reviewed.
International Students: The “Foreign Transcript Evaluation” item on the checklist prompts us to do an evaluation of your non-U.S. academic work after your transcripts have been received. It is an internal processing item; you do not need to do anything to complete it. You do not need to ask a third-party credential evaluator to review your transcripts.
PhD Application Deadlines:
Spring Admission: September 1 at 10pm MST.
Please Note: We admit very few students for the Spring semester and focus more on Fall admissions. We do not recommend applying for Spring unless specifically requested by an ECEE faculty member.
Fall Admission:
International Applications: December 10 at 10pm MST.
U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents: December 15 at 10pm MST.
PhD Application Decisions Released:
Spring Admission: You will be notified of your application decision by mid-October.
Fall Admission: You will be notified of your application decision by mid-March.
All Master's Degree Program Application Deadlines:
Spring Admission: September 1 at 10pm MST.
Deadlines are the same for U.S. citizens, permanent residents and international applicants.
Fall Admission: February 15 at 10pm MST.
Deadlines are the same for U.S. citizens, permanent residents and international applicants.
All Master's Degree Program Decisions Released:
Spring Admission: You will be notified of your application decision by end of October.
Fall Admission: You will be notified of your application decision by early April.
Minimum Eligibility Requirement (PhD & Master's)
Our minimum eligibility requirement to apply to either the PhD or MS programs is a GPA of 3.0 of higher from an accredited Bachelor of Science (BS) STEM program, preferably in Engineering or Natural/Physical Sciences.
Please Note: Admission to our graduate programs is competitive, and GPA is one of many factors reviewed in the application process. Meeting the minimum eligibility requirement does not guarantee admission.
Applicants do not need to apply separately for funding or secure funding/an advisor in advance of applying.
Prerequisite Coursework
We do not require an applicant has specific prerequisite coursework to apply for our MS or PhD degrees. We will review any applicant who meets our minimum eligibility requirements.
We do recommend visiting the list of minors our Department offers: https://www.colorado.edu/ecee/academics/undergraduate-programs/minor-programs and reviewing the coursework listed as a helpful guide to determine if an applicant has the general base knowledge for our graduate programs. We do not require a minor or any of these specific courses be completed to apply.
Application Requirements (PhD and Master's)
Complete the Online Application.
If you have any issues with the online application, email technical support at gradadm@colorado.edu.
Pay the application fee: $60 for domestic applicants or $80 for international applicants. We cannot process your application without the application fee.
If you are an international applicant, submit your English proficiency test scores. Refer to the CU Boulder English Proficiency Requirements for details.
Contact information/email addresses for the three persons who will supply your three letters of recommendation.
Secured links are sent directly to recommenders once you add their information and click the 'Send to Recommender' button in the application.
You should submit your application at least two weeks prior to the posted deadline so recommendation letters can be received by the application deadline.
We will only accept three recommenders. Please do not input more than three recommenders in the application.
Letters from former instructors are preferred. If you are a PhD applicant, letters from those who can evaluate your research ability are helpful. Letters from work supervisors and/or work colleagues are also acceptable, especially if you have spent time working in industry/out of academia.
Upload unofficial copies of your transcripts.
We require transcripts from each undergraduate and graduate institution you attended, including community colleges, summer sessions, and extension programs. While credits from one institution may appear on the transcript of a second institution, unofficial transcripts must be submitted from each institution, regardless of the length of attendance, and whether or not courses were completed. Failure to list and submit transcripts from all institutions previously attended is considered to be a violation of academic ethics and may result in the cancellation of your admission or dismissal from the university.
International Applicants: You do not need to ask a third-party credential evaluator, such as WES, to review your transcripts. Our International Admissions Team is able to evaluate your transcript without any additional service needed.
If you are admitted, you must then submit official transcripts from these same institutions.
Upload your Statement of Purpose.
This statement should be no longer than 750 words and should address your academic and career goals and how CU Boulder fits within those goals.
Please adhere to the word limit. Be concise and direct.
The GRE is not required for our application process. Submitting these scores does not have any added benefit as the GRE is not part of the review process.
Applicants do not need to apply separately for funding or secure funding/an advisor in advance of applying.
Fee Waivers
Fee Waiver Information, Master's Applicants:
The Graduate School has fee waiver information available here. This includes fee waivers for eligible U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
We do not have fee waivers available for international applicants.
Fee Waiver Information, PhD Applicants:
The College offers application fee waivers as listed until November 15 annually. This includes fee waivers for eligible U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
The Graduate School has fee waiver information available here. This includes fee waivers for eligible U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
We do not have fee waivers available for international applicants.
Funding Your Degree
PhD Applicants: Applicants do not need to apply separately for funding or secure funding/an advisor in advance of applying. Our admitted PhD students are offered Research Assistantships with five years of funding, unless the applicant has other stated means (tuition remission with employer, home country government scholarships, external fellowship, etc.). A Research Assistantship provides a stipend, tuition remission of up to ten credits each in the Fall and Spring semesters, and 91% of the student health insurance premium, which includes dental insurance. Summer is not included in our offer. Funding is renewed each semester based upon satisfactory performance and the availability of funds.
For AY 2026-2027 the monthly stipend rate is $3,460.25.
Master's Applicants:The department does not provide funding for master’s students. Master’s students should plan on providing their own fellowships and/or private funds to finance their education.
Possible funding sources may include student loans, outside fellowships, employer sponsorships, etc.
Some funding information/opportunities may be found on the Graduate School's funding website.
The CU Office of Financial Aid has full information on federal programs for domestic graduate students, eligibility, and what you need to do apply.
The College of Engineering & Applied Science hosted a webinar on funding a master's degree; the slides and recording can be accessed here:
Recording of the Paying for Graduate School Information session
Slides
ECEE does not use Teaching Assistantships. Instead, we hire hourly course support student roles which both traditional and professional MS students are eligible for. Research Assistantships are generally reserved for PhD students and are rarely available to master's students. Research positions are not centrally managed. Students must reach out directly to faculty to find research opportunities. Professional MS students are not eligible for Teaching Assistantship or Research Assistantship roles; only traditional MS students are eligible if positions become available.
Student employment can also be found throughout campus.
Tuition costs differ between the professional master's program and traditional MS program; additional tuition differences apply due to in-state or out-of-state residency. For more information, visit the Bursar:
